---
title: "Templates"
---

Word templates for every step from question to publication, in the Neudata house style. They are generic: replace `[Institution]`, `[Ethics committee name]` and the other `[grey placeholders]` with your own details. Each Word file has a matching PDF for printing.

| File | Purpose | Used in | Download |
|:--------------|:--------------------------------------------|:--------------|:----------|
| **Research proposal template** | The group proposal and publication plan, built in four parts. **Part 1** covers the working title, problem, PICO, question, FINER, objectives and references. **Part 2** covers design, population, outcomes and bias. **Part 3** covers variables, the mini-CRF, data dictionary, data management and quality plan, sample size, analysis plan and missing-data plan. **Part 4** covers ethics and consent, registration, confidentiality, feasibility (Gantt, budget, recruitment) and a publication plan: target journal and reporting guideline, authorship and CRediT roles, working title and a structured-abstract skeleton. Every section has guidance, a running-example illustration and a placeholder. The finished proposal should be about 6–8 pages. | Part 1 S1–S2 · Part 2 S3–S4 · Part 3 S5–S6 · Part 4 S7 · presented in S8 | [Word](files/templates/Research_Proposal_Template.docx) · [PDF](files/templates/Research_Proposal_Template.pdf) |
| **Literature review worksheet** | Turns the PICO into a search-terms grid (synonyms, MeSH, Boolean). Includes a search log, an evidence matrix (landscape) with two worked rows from the course papers, a "known / gap" summary and five key references. | S2 (2.1 Finding the evidence, 2.4 literature matrix; proposal Part 1) | [Word](files/templates/Literature_Review_Worksheet.docx) · [PDF](files/templates/Literature_Review_Worksheet.pdf) |
| **CRF + data dictionary template** | A case report form built on good CRF design principles, with example items for the running example: eligibility, demographics, SOFA and lactate, daily fluids in and out with cumulative balance (ml/kg), and day-28 vital status. A data dictionary follows on a landscape page. | S5 (5.1 Good data by design; proposal Part 3) | [Word](files/templates/CRF_Template.docx) · [PDF](files/templates/CRF_Template.pdf) |
| **Statistical analysis plan template** | SAP written before data lock, with 14 sections: summary and objectives; outcome definitions; analysis populations; descriptive analysis (Table 1); primary analysis; secondary analyses; confounders and adjustment; pre-specified subgroups and interaction; multiple comparisons; missing data (assessment, complete-case vs imputation, sensitivity); sample size; software; table and figure shells; version history and sign-off. The guidance uses the running example, and a worked SAP for the course dataset is in [SAP for FLUID-ICU](sap.qmd). | S6 (6.4; proposal Part 3) | [Word](files/templates/Statistical_Analysis_Plan_Template.docx) · [PDF](files/templates/Statistical_Analysis_Plan_Template.pdf) |
| **Study protocol template** | SPIRIT-style protocol for an observational study or a simple trial: administrative information, synopsis, background, objectives, design, participants, interventions/exposures, outcomes, schedule of assessments, sample size, allocation/blinding, data management, statistics, monitoring/safety, ethics/consent, confidentiality, dissemination, funding, references and appendices. | S7 (7.1 Protocol, ethics and consent); take-home | [Word](files/templates/Study_Protocol_Template.docx) · [PDF](files/templates/Study_Protocol_Template.pdf) |
| **Informed consent template** | A plain-language participant information sheet (13 question headings) and consent form. It covers initials boxes, signatures for the participant, the person taking consent, an impartial witness and a legal representative, and continuing (deferred) consent. Guidance boxes cover readability and ICU or emergency consent. | S7 (7.1); take-home | [Word](files/templates/Informed_Consent_Template.docx) · [PDF](files/templates/Informed_Consent_Template.pdf) |
| **Manuscript template (IMRaD)** | An original-research manuscript. It contains a title page, structured abstract and keywords, then an Introduction (3-paragraph funnel) and Methods with subheadings. Results start with participant flow; the Discussion follows six moves (answer, compare, explain, limitations, implications, conclude), then the Conclusion. Declarations cover ethics, consent, registration, funding, competing interests, data availability, AI use and a CRediT contribution grid. References, table shells and a flow-diagram shell follow, plus a reporting-guideline reminder box (CONSORT, STROBE, STARD, PRISMA, EQUATOR). Groups use it for their FLUID-ICU course-dataset manuscript ([manuscript brief](manuscript-brief.qmd)). | S7 (7.3, Methods + Results) and S8 (8.1, rest of the draft) | [Word](files/templates/Manuscript_Template_IMRaD.docx) · [PDF](files/templates/Manuscript_Template_IMRaD.pdf) |
| **Cover letter template** | A one-page journal cover letter on a letterhead block for your institution. It has placeholders for the question, main finding, why this journal, and the standard statements (originality, ethics, registration, reporting checklist, competing interests). Optional suggested reviewers. | S8 (8.2 Getting published) | [Word](files/templates/Cover_Letter_Template.docx) · [PDF](files/templates/Cover_Letter_Template.pdf) |
| **Response-to-reviewers template** | Tone and method guidance, a letter to the editor, three worked fictional rows (two agreements and one polite disagreement), and point-by-point tables (comment / response / change made with page and line) for the editor and two reviewers. | S8 (8.2); peer-review swap after S8 | [Word](files/templates/Response_to_Reviewers_Template.docx) · [PDF](files/templates/Response_to_Reviewers_Template.pdf) |
| **Conference abstract and poster template** | A 250–300-word structured abstract with word budgets per section and a fictional example. Page 2 is a poster layout guide: a three-column grid sketch and rules for text size, words, figures and colours. | S8 (8.2) | [Word](files/templates/Conference_Abstract_Template.docx) · [PDF](files/templates/Conference_Abstract_Template.pdf) |

**Tips.** Use **Ctrl + H → Find `[`** to step through the placeholders. To delete all the grey guidance at once: **Home → Styles**, right-click **Guidance** (or **Example**), **Select All**, **Delete**. For a consent form, cover letter or manuscript, replace the Neudata header with your institution's letterhead or the journal's format.
